assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy is a rare chain from basic hormone biology (proglucagon processing, insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36), receptor biology) to drugs that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Importance, originality and societal impact are exceptional, and the physiological insight (gut-pancreas-brain endocrine signaling) is clean and clearly integrative.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1) and Drucker (receptor biology, intestinotropic and cardiometabolic actions, translation) are strong basic contributors; Mojsov's early peptide chemistry and demonstration of GLP-1 activity is a key but historically contested contribution. Knudsen is the leading drug-development figure, but I judge the basic discovery trio more defensible for a Nobel configuration; the allocation across basic and translational contributors is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed by large randomized outcome trials and broad clinical adoption; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for the early GLP-1 characterization (Mojsov, Habener and others) is disputed and the supplied list may not capture all contributors.
Whether the committee prefers to recognize the translational drug developer (Knudsen) over a basic-science configuration is open.
I have not independently verified the details of the priority history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity with millisecond precision, from channelrhodopsin discovery to its use in circuits, behavior and disease models. It is highly original and has reshaped how circuit function, including motor and locomotor circuits, is dissected across species. The method is a tool but the discovery of light-gated channels and their transfer to neurons is a defensible invention-level prize.
assessment.attribution: Nagel, Hegemann (with Bamberg) identified and characterized channelrhodopsins; Deisseroth and Boyden demonstrated neuronal use, and Miesenboeck contributed early genetically encoded photoactivation. With at most three laureates, any selection omits major contributors; I pick the two channelrhodopsin discoverers plus Deisseroth for broad neuroscience adoption. Credit between Boyden and Deisseroth and the role of Bamberg are genuinely unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Widely and independently reproduced for over a decade; clinical translation (e.g. vision restoration) is only emerging but the methodological impact is established and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Six credited names cannot fit within three laureates; the allocation is contentious.
Clinical translational evidence is still early.
Prior Nobel recognition of related tools may shape committee appetite for a methods prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation is the best-studied cellular model of synaptic plasticity and underpins the modern synaptic framework for learning and memory. The 1973 discovery, the NMDA-receptor dependence and the later behavioral links form a coherent and lasting body of work with large conceptual impact.
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo made the original discovery; Collingridge established NMDA-receptor dependence, a key mechanistic step. Morris linked NMDA-dependent plasticity to spatial learning behavior and could be preferred by some members; the choice between Collingridge and Morris is a real allocation issue.
assessment.maturity: Over fifty years of confirmation and thoroughly mature, though the causal claim that LTP is the memory trace remains debated, which tempers but does not remove timeliness; senior age of laureates adds urgency.
uncertainties: Whether LTP is demonstrably the substrate of memory rather than a correlate is still argued.
Collingridge versus Morris for the third place.
Lømo and Bliss are elderly; I cannot verify current status.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living drugs. The clinical impact is major and the engineering concept of combining antibody specificity with T-cell signaling is original.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain led design of costimulated CAR constructs and the first durable clinical responses; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early engineered-T-cell clinical trials. The original CAR concept (Eshhar and colleagues) is not in the supplied credit, which complicates a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and multiple independent trials confirm efficacy; toxicity, access and limited efficacy in solid tumors remain, but the principle is established.
uncertainties: The supplied credit may omit the originator of the chimeric receptor concept.
Efficacy in solid tumors and long-term safety remain unresolved.
Rosenberg's contribution is adoptive transfer more broadly than CAR specifically.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and the targeting of BCR-ABL turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable one and validated kinase inhibition as a general paradigm in oncology. The proof of concept is exceptionally clear and impactful.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development), Druker (clinical translation and trials) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a natural trio; the discoverers of the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL fusion are not in the supplied credit and chemistry contributors are partly omitted.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of clinical outcome data and independent confirmation; recognition is mature but translation-focused configurations can be questioned for basic originality.
uncertainties: Basic-discovery lineage (Philadelphia chromosome, BCR-ABL fusion) falls outside the supplied names.
Industrial medicinal-chemistry contributions may be undercredited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The linking of dopamine neuron activity to reward prediction error and temporal-difference learning is a rare case where recordings in primates and a computational theory converged, with influence on learning theory, addiction, psychiatry and AI. I view it as strong and conceptually elegant, evaluated on the evidence rather than on any familiarity with neural circuits.
assessment.attribution: Schultz made the decisive neurophysiological observations; Dayan and Montague, with Sejnowski (not listed), formalized the dopamine-TD-learning link. Dolan's contribution is human imaging. Four names exceed the limit and the theoretical credit is shared among people outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Replicated across species and methods, including optogenetic tests; interpretation has been refined (e.g. alternative accounts of dopamine function) but the core finding is stable.
uncertainties: Dopamine's role beyond pure prediction error is debated.
Theoretical credit assignment partly lies outside the supplied names.
Clinical translation is indirect.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of orexin/hypocretin and its loss in narcolepsy type 1 explained a major sleep disorder at the molecular level and opened the path to orexin receptor antagonists and agonists. The convergence of peptide discovery and canine and human genetics is compelling physiology.
assessment.attribution: Sakurai and Yanagisawa identified orexins and their receptors; de Lecea and Kilduff independently found hypocretin; Mignot's positional cloning of the canine narcolepsy gene and human studies established the disease link. Priority between orexin and hypocretin groups is an unresolved allocation issue.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed; clinical drugs (suvorexant and others) exist, and agonists are in trials. Recognition appears timely.
uncertainties: Parallel discovery by two groups complicates attribution.
Which of Mignot or de Lecea best completes the trio is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent infection and cervical and other cancers, with population-level evidence of dramatic reductions in disease. The conceptual step of self-assembling L1 capsid particles is original and its public-health impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLP immunogenicity; Frazer (with Zhou) produced VLPs and early vaccine work. Other contributors (e.g. Zhou, Kirnbauer, Georgetown group) are outside the list, so allocation is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by large trials and national registries; mature. The 2008 prize for HPV linkage to cancer may affect committee appetite for another HPV-related prize.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over VLP production among several groups.
Prior Nobel recognition of the HPV-cancer link may reduce appetite.
Supplied names omit some key contributors.
